steps.prompt_exact: Build me a tiny train platform dispatcher as a single-file HTML game: it should be easy to understand fast, let me route arriving trains into platforms under time pressure, and run with no external assets.
steps.response_exact:
Claude responded: Here's how to play:VUnable to reach visualizeHere's how to play:
Select a train from the arrivals panel — click it once to highlight it. Then click an empty platform to route it there. That's the whole loop.
A few things to watch:

The colored dot on each train card is your urgency signal — green → amber → red as its time runs out. The thin bar below shrinks as it approaches departure.
The top-right timer bar tracks your most urgent arrival's remaining time.
Trains dwell for ~7 seconds after routing, then the platform clears automatically.
Miss 5 trains and the station closes.
Every 30 seconds the level ticks up, trains arrive faster and TTLs shorten — routing quickly earns bonus points based on how much time you had left.

Done — zero external refs, confirmed. Here's what changed:

Keyboard controls

1–7 — select an arrival by its position in the queue (badge shown on each card)
F / J / K — assign selected train to Platform 1 / 2 / 3 (key shown in each platform header)
Esc — deselect current train
Enter or Space — restart from the game-over screen
All platform and train cards are also tabindex="0" with Enter/Space activation for full keyboard-only play

Mobile layout (≤ 480px / 390px)

HUD splits into two rows: 3 stats on top, urgency bar + level badge below — no 5-column squeeze
Platforms stay 3-column but with tighter padding that fits at 390px without overflow
Key badges and the hint bar are hidden on touch screens (they'd just clutter a small display)
section-hint labels hidden on mobile to recover horizontal space
align-items: flex-start on body so tall content scrolls rather than overflows
